meta.title: Graphs of Piecewise Linear Functions
meta.pageTitle: Graphs of Piecewise Linear Functions | Hesten's Learning
meta.description: Define appropriate quantities from physical situations, choose logical scales, and translate actions into piecewise graphs.
meta.pageDescription: Learn how to define quantities, choose scales, and translate physical actions into piecewise graphs with interactive stories.
meta.author: Hesten's Learning Team

overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 1
overview.text: In this lesson, you will learn to define appropriate quantities from physical situations, choose logical scales, and translate actions into piecewise graphs. Explore the interactive ladder simulation below, and read the classroom discussion blocks to master these concepts.
outcomes: Define appropriate variables to represent a physical situation.
Choose and interpret the scale and origin for a coordinate plane.
Understand that the slope of each line segment represents the average rate of change.
overview.teacherInsight: If students struggle, physically act out the story. Place tape on the floor and have them walk forward (positive slope), stand still (zero slope), and walk backward (negative slope) while drawing the graph together.

content.title: Animated Ladder Descent
content.desc: Observe the physical elevation of the climber as he descends and pauses.
content.graphDesc: Watch the live synchronized marker trace the slope changes on the piecewise graph.

content.title: Teacher Guide Concepts: Deepen Your Understanding

concepts.title: Concept 1: Is a 2.5 ft/min Descent Speed Realistic on a Ladder?
concepts.text: In Example 1 of the teacher materials, students analyze a graph with a slope representing $2.5\text{ ft/min}$. While mathematically sound, a rate of $2.5\text{ ft/min}$ is incredibly slow for a person physically moving down a standard ladder (about $0.5\text{ inches per second}$). If we shift the horizontal unit of time from minutes to seconds, a speed of $2.5\text{ ft/sec}$ becomes perfectly realistic for a steady descent.

concepts.title: Concept 2: Calculating Average Rate of Change
concepts.text: To compute the average rate of change over any interval, use the change in elevation divided by the change in time:
concepts.formula: Average Rate of Change = \frac{\Delta \text{Elevation}}{\Delta \text{Time}} = \frac{h(t_2) - h(t_1)}{t_2 - t_1}
concepts.example: For instance, between $t = 0$ and $t = 6$ seconds on our ladder descent: $\frac{3 - 10}{6 - 0} = \frac{-7}{6} \approx -1.17\text{ ft/sec}$. This negative rate represents a descent. When discussing descent speed, we refer to its absolute value: $1.17\text{ ft/sec}$.

concepts.title: Concept 3: The 9 Distinct Time Intervals of the Video Story
concepts.text: In the lesson Exit Ticket, teachers analyze the full video of a man traversing stairs and platforms, which features nine distinct linear segments. Segmenting graphs into non-overlapping time intervals is a vital skill. Here are the exact nine time intervals identified in the curriculum guide:

content.title: Design Your Own Piecewise Graphing Story
content.desc: Modify each step of the journey and watch the custom graph below transform accordingly.

content.title: Visual Study Guides
content.desc: Toggle tabs below to explore interactive visual explainers of core concepts.

vocabulary.definition: A function defined by multiple linear segments, each covering a specific interval of time or domain. The overall graph looks like joined straight lines with corners.
The change in the dependent variable (elevation) divided by the change in the independent variable (time) over a given interval. Graphically, this is the slope of the line segment.
The input value of a function, which changes independently (usually time, graphed on the horizontal axis).
The output value of a function, which depends on the input value (usually elevation/height, graphed on the vertical axis).

practiceQuestions.question: A climber ascends 4 feet in 2 seconds, pauses for 3 seconds, then descends 2 feet in 1 second. What is the slope of the graph during the 3-second pause?
practiceQuestions.explanation: During a pause, elevation remains unchanged while time advances. Rate of change (Δy / Δt) = 0 / 3 = 0.

practiceQuestions.question: On an elevation-versus-time graph, what physical action does a segment with a negative slope depict?
options: The climber is stationary at rest
The climber is ascending to higher rungs
The climber is descending towards the ground
The climber has completed the entire climb
practiceQuestions.explanation: A negative slope means the elevation quantity is decreasing over time, representing a physical descent.

Growing from $s=2$ to $s=3$ adds 5 units of area ($9 - 4$).
Growing from $s=9$ to $s=10$ adds 19 units of area ($100 - 81$).

meta.title: Order of Operations & Absolute Value with Rational Numbers
meta.pageTitle: Order of Operations & Absolute Value | GED Math | Hesten's Learning
meta.description: Master the hierarchy of arithmetic operations (PEMDAS / GEMDAS), absolute value distance properties, and operations with signed rational numbers for the GED Quantitative Reasoning test.
meta.pageDescription: Comprehensive GED Math prep on Order of Operations, absolute value distance properties, nested grouping, and signed rational numbers without a calculator.
meta.author: Hesten's Learning GED Team

overview.title: Student & Educator Overview: Quantitative Arithmetic
overview.text: On the official GED Mathematical Reasoning exam, the first 5 questions are administered in Part 1 without the TI-30XS calculator. A fluent command of the Order of Operations (PEMDAS/GEMDAS), absolute value distance logic, and signed rational arithmetic is essential to securing early high-value points toward passing (145+) and college readiness (165+).
outcomes: Apply the universal hierarchy of operations (PEMDAS/GEMDAS) with grouping symbols, nested parentheses, and fraction bars.
Interpret absolute value |x| as non-negative distance on the real number line, simplifying expressions like 4 - 2|3 - 8| + 3².
Eliminate sign and exponent pitfalls, accurately distinguishing between -x² and (-x)² when working with negative rational numbers.
overview.teacherInsight: Remind students that absolute value bars act as grouping symbols: evaluate the interior expression completely before taking the absolute value. Emphasize that -4² = -(4 · 4) = -16, whereas (-4)² = (-4)(-4) = +16.

content.html:
Interactive GEMDAS Hierarchy Explorer

Step through the official GED evaluation sequence for nested arithmetic expressions.

1. Grouping Symbols (G)Parentheses $( )$, brackets $[ ]$, absolute value $| \dots |$, and radical signs $\sqrt{\dots}$. Also includes implied numerator/denominator groups in fraction bars $\frac{A}{B}$.
2. Exponents & Radicals (E)Powers like $3^2 = 9$ or $(-2)^3 = -8$. Note that $-5^2 = -(5^2) = -25$, while $(-5)^2 = +25$.
3. Multiplication & Division (M / D)Equal rank! Computed strictly left-to-right as they appear: $12 \div 3 \cdot 2 = 4 \cdot 2 = 8$.
4. Addition & Subtraction (A / S)Equal rank! Computed strictly left-to-right: $7 - 10 + 4 = -3 + 4 = 1$.
Worked GED Benchmark Example:
Evaluate: $$E = 4 - 2 \cdot |3 - 8| + 3^2$$
  1. Inside Absolute Value: $3 - 8 = -5 \implies 4 - 2 \cdot |-5| + 3^2$
  2. Absolute Value Evaluation: $|-5| = 5 \implies 4 - 2 \cdot (5) + 3^2$
  3. Exponents: $3^2 = 9 \implies 4 - 2 \cdot 5 + 9$
  4. Multiplication: $2 \cdot 5 = 10 \implies 4 - 10 + 9$
  5. Left-to-Right Add / Subtract: $4 - 10 = -6$, then $-6 + 9 = \mathbf{3}$.

content.title: Core GED Test Principles & Common Traps

concepts.title: Concept 1: Absolute Value as Geometric Distance
concepts.text: In geometry and real analysis, the absolute value $|a - b|$ represents the distance between points $a$ and $b$ on the coordinate line. Because distance is scalar and non-negative, $|x| \ge 0$ for every real number $x$. When subtracting integers under absolute value bars, $|3 - 8| = |-5| = 5$, and $|8 - 3| = |5| = 5$. Notice the order inside does not change the physical distance between 3 and 8.

concepts.title: Concept 2: The Fraction Bar as an Implied Grouping Barrier
concepts.text: When an algebraic or rational expression has operations in the numerator and denominator, such as $\frac{-18 + 6}{-2^2 + 1}$, the fraction bar creates an invisible set of parentheses around both parts: $[ -18 + 6 ] \div [ -2^2 + 1 ]$. Never divide prematurely before completely simplifying both the top and bottom terms independently.

concepts.title: Concept 3: The $-x^2$ vs $(-x)^2$ Sign Trap
concepts.text: This is one of the most frequently missed question types on Part 1 of the GED Math test. In $-3^2$, the base of the exponent is only $3$. The exponent takes precedence before multiplication by $-1$: $-3^2 = -(3 \cdot 3) = -9$. Conversely, in $(-3)^2$, the parentheses declare that the entire quantity $-3$ is the base: $(-3)^2 = (-3) \cdot (-3) = +9$.

vocabulary.definition: The universal convention for evaluating mathematical expressions: Grouping symbols → Exponents → Multiplication & Division (left to right) → Addition & Subtraction (left to right).
The non-negative distance between a number and zero on the real number line, written as |x|. For any real number, |-a| = |a| = a (where a ≥ 0).
Any number that can be expressed as a quotient or fraction a/b of two integers, with non-zero denominator b. Includes integers, fractions, terminating decimals, and repeating decimals.
In b^n, b is the base and n is the exponent. Note that -a^n = -(a^n) retains the negative sign, whereas (-a)^n with an even exponent yields a positive result.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the value of the arithmetic expression: $$4 - 2 \cdot |3 - 8| + 3^2$$
practiceQuestions.explanation: Step 1: Simplify inside the absolute value bars: $3 - 8 = -5$. Step 2: Evaluate the absolute value: $|-5| = 5$. Step 3: Evaluate the exponent: $3^2 = 9$. Step 4: Multiply: $2 \cdot 5 = 10$. Step 5: Add and subtract from left to right: $4 - 10 + 9 = -6 + 9 = 3$.

practiceQuestions.question: Simplify the rational algebraic fraction: $$\frac{-18 + 6}{-2^2 + 1}$$
practiceQuestions.explanation: Simplify the numerator: $-18 + 6 = -12$. In the denominator, evaluate the exponent first: $-2^2 = -(2^2) = -4$. Then $-4 + 1 = -3$. Finally, divide the numerator by denominator: $\frac{-12}{-3} = +4$.

practiceQuestions.question: A marine research vessel records a submarine at an initial depth of $-42\text{ meters}$. The vessel ascends $18\text{ meters}$, then descends $25\text{ meters}$. What is the submarine's final depth, and what was its total vertical distance traveled?
options: Final depth: $-49\text{ m}$; Total distance: $43\text{ m}$
Final depth: $-49\text{ m}$; Total distance: $85\text{ m}$
Final depth: $-35\text{ m}$; Total distance: $43\text{ m}$
Final depth: $-49\text{ m}$; Total distance: $49\text{ m}$
practiceQuestions.explanation: Final depth combines signed values: $-42 + 18 - 25 = -24 - 25 = -49\text{ m}$. Total vertical distance traveled is the sum of the absolute value of each leg of travel: $|+18| + |-25| = 18 + 25 = 43\text{ m}$.
